AAPL.rationale: Apple presents a fundamentally strong profile with accelerating YoY growth (revenue +16.6%, EPS +21.8% in Q2 FY2026), broad-based margin expansion (net margin from 0.243 to 0.272, gross margin at 49.3%), robust cash generation ($28.7B OCF in Q2, $82.6B H1), and a rapidly improving balance sheet (D/E from ~1.42 to 0.78). Services revenue at $31B quarterly with ~76% gross margins is the primary margin driver. The franchise is best-in-class: 2.5B active devices, ~90% iPhone retention, and market share gains across all hardware segments (iPhone volume 19%→21%, revenue share 43%→48%). Valuation is the key constraint: P/E of 35.8x has compressed from 43.1x peak but still demands sustained high-teens growth, and the earnings yield of 2.8% sits well below the 10Y Treasury at 4.46%, implying a negative equity risk premium. The stock is cheaper on an earnings-power basis than six months ago despite better fundamentals — a constructive setup. Near-term catalysts are modest: WWDC AI reaction has stabilized (stock recovered from initial selloff), the $100B buyback authorization provides support, and Tim Cook's pricing-power signal on memory costs is a credible margin defense. However, the flattening yield curve (10Y-2Y at 0.27%) signals recession risk that could pressure consumer hardware demand, and the negative ERP leaves little margin of safety. The score reflects strong fundamentals and trajectory (pillar 1) partially offset by a still-elevated absolute multiple (pillar 2), with a modest positive bump from the WWDC stabilization and buyback catalyst (pillar 3).
